chapters.title: Chapter 1: Linear Algebra Foundations for Attention
chapters.description: Covers the linear algebra operations and identities that underlie attention: matrix multiplications, transposes, dot-products, scaling, and row-wise operations. Introduces notation and the matrix view of batched multi-head computations.
subtopics: Matrix and vector operations (multiply, transpose, dot-product)
Batch and block matrix views
Row-wise operations and reductions (rowmax, rowsum)
Block matrices and tiling notation
Scaling factors and normalization (e.g., 1/sqrt(d))
Basic properties used in attention algebra (distributivity, associativity)

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Transformer and Multi-Head Attention
chapters.description: Explains the Transformer architecture's attention mechanism, multi-head attention, masking, and how attention fits into encoder/decoder layers and large language models.
subtopics: Self-attention: queries (Q), keys (K), values (V) and attention output
Multi-head attention: parallel heads and concatenation
Scaling and softmax application (row-wise softmax)
Causal (autoregressive) masking vs. non-causal attention
Computation graph and where attention sits in Transformer blocks
Practical dimensions: batch, sequence length, head dimension, hidden dimension

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Differentiation and Backpropagation of Attention
chapters.description: Derives the backward pass for attention and explains recomputation and memory/computation trade-offs in computing gradients for attention layers.
subtopics: Chain rule applied to attention: dO → dV, dP, dS, dQ, dK
Derivative of softmax (vector Jacobian-product form)
Efficient formulations of attention gradients (matrix forms)
Recomputation vs. storing intermediates: trade-offs
Implications for memory usage and computational cost in backward pass

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Numerical Analysis and Stability (Softmax and Exponentials)
chapters.description: Examines numerical stability issues in softmax and exponential computations, common tricks to improve stability, and error propagation in chained operations.
subtopics: Numerical issues with exponentials and overflow/underflow
Rowwise max subtraction (log-sum-exp trick)
Precision and accumulation error basics
Stability of softmax and mitigation techniques
Error propagation through matmuls and reductions

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Floating-Point Formats and Low-Precision Arithmetic
chapters.description: Introduces floating-point formats used in machine learning hardware, their dynamic ranges and precision, and the implications for computation and accumulation.
subtopics: IEEE-754 basics and FP32 semantics
Half-precision formats: FP16 vs BF16 (representation and tradeoffs)
Emerging low-precision formats: FP8 variants (e4m3, e5m2) and reduced mantissa/exponent tradeoffs
Rounding modes, subnormal numbers, infinities and NaNs
Mixed-precision computation and accumulator precision

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Quantization Techniques and Error Metrics
chapters.description: Covers practical quantization approaches for tensors, scaling strategies, handling outliers, and metrics to evaluate quantization accuracy.
subtopics: Per-tensor vs per-channel/per-block quantization
Static vs dynamic range scaling
Block quantization and its motivations
Stochastic/biased quantization variants
Error metrics: RMSE, relative error, worst-case error
Strategies for handling outlier activations

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Randomized and Fast Orthogonal Transforms
chapters.description: Introduces randomized orthogonal transforms used to reduce quantization error and spread out outliers, with efficient algorithms and properties.
subtopics: Orthogonal matrices and invariance properties (M M^T = I)
Random diagonal sign matrices and their effect
Hadamard transform: definition and fast O(d log d) implementation
Structured random orthogonal transforms (signs + Hadamard)
Use-cases: incoherent processing and reducing quantization error

chapters.title: Chapter 8: GPU Architecture and Memory Hierarchy
chapters.description: Presents the hardware building blocks of modern GPUs relevant to attention: streaming multiprocessors, shared memory, caches, registers, and global memory hierarchy.
subtopics: Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) and their resources
Memory hierarchy: global memory (HBM), L2 cache, shared memory (SMEM), registers
Bandwidth vs capacity trade-offs across memory tiers
Banking, bank conflicts, and memory coalescing
Latency hiding through concurrency

chapters.title: Chapter 9: GPU Programming Model and Thread Hierarchy
chapters.description: Explains threads, warps, CTAs/blocks, warpgroups, occupancy, scheduling, and the mapping of parallel work to hardware resources.
subtopics: CUDA execution model: threads, warps (32 threads), blocks (CTAs), grids
Warp and block scheduling on SMs
Occupancy: registers, shared memory, and maximum active warps
Cooperative groups and cluster scheduling concepts
Register allocation limits and their impact on kernel configuration

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Asynchrony, Concurrency, and Software Pipelining on GPUs
chapters.description: Describes asynchronous hardware features and how software designs overlap computation and data movement to hide latency; introduces double buffering and software pipelining concepts.
subtopics: Asynchronous units on GPUs (separate units for compute, memory engines)
Overlapping data movement and computation (producer-consumer patterns)
Double buffering, circular buffers and ping-pong buffers (general patterns)
Software pipelining across iterations
Trade-offs: register pressure, synchronization, and pipeline depth

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Synchronization, Barriers, and Cooperative Primitives
chapters.description: Explains intra-CTA and inter-warp synchronization primitives and patterns used to coordinate data movement and computation on GPUs.
subtopics: __syncthreads vs fine-grained barrier instructions (bar.sync)
Producer-consumer coordination and commit/wait semantics
Atomic operations and memory ordering constraints
CUDA cooperative groups and barrier variants
Impacts of synchronization on performance and latency hiding

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Tensor Cores and Matrix-Multiply Engines
chapters.description: Details specialized matrix multiplication units (Tensor Cores), their programming interfaces, tiling, operand/accumulator layouts, and precision modes.
subtopics: Overview of Tensor Cores and hardware-accelerated matmul
Tile-based matmul decomposition and GEMM primitives
Programming interfaces: WMMA/WGMMA concepts (tile sizes, operands, accumulators)
Operand layout constraints (mn-major vs k-major) and accumulation semantics
Precision modes supported by Tensor Cores (FP16/BF16/FP8) and performance implications

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Specialized Memory Engines and Data Movement Instructions
chapters.description: Covers dedicated memory acceleration units and specialized instructions for efficient tile loads/stores and in-register/register-memory transfers.
subtopics: Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) / async high-performance copy engines
LDSM and STSM (ldmatrix / stmatrix) style warp-level matrix load/store
Byte-permute and shuffle instructions for register rearrangement
Coalesced load/store strategies and in-kernel transpose basics
When to use pre-processing transpose vs in-kernel transpose

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Memory Tiling, Blocking Strategies and Buffer Management
chapters.description: Explains tiling strategies for matmul and attention to maximize data reuse, reduce global memory traffic, and manage on-chip buffers (shared memory, circular buffers).
subtopics: Tile sizes for queries, keys, values (block sizes in sequence and head dimensions)
Blocking for compute vs blocking for memory bandwidth
Circular/shared memory buffering and multi-stage buffering
Producer/consumer partitioning of warps and buffer life-cycle
Register tiling and exchanging intermediate tiles across stages

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Implementing Softmax Efficiently on GPUs
chapters.description: Focuses on GPU-friendly softmax implementations: numerically stable reductions, approximations of exponential, and reducing special-function bottlenecks.
subtopics: Row-wise reduction patterns (max, sum) implemented in parallel
Numerically stable softmax: subtracting row max and log-sum-exp
Efficient evaluation of exponentials and special function unit constraints
Approximation methods for exponentials and trade-offs
Minimizing memory traffic when computing softmax (local reductions)

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Kernel Fusion, Operator Fusion, and Memory Elimination
chapters.description: Describes strategies to fuse multiple operators into a single kernel to eliminate intermediate global memory reads/writes and reduce bandwidth pressure.
subtopics: Principles of operator fusion and staged fusion patterns
Benefits of fusing matmul + softmax + matmul in attention
Trade-offs: code complexity, register pressure, and compiler effects
Local (block) reductions enabling fused softmax
Examples of fused kernels in ML workloads (general patterns)

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Performance Measurement, Profiling, and Benchmarking on GPUs
chapters.description: Outlines how to quantify performance for GPU kernels: FLOPs accounting, utilization metrics, profiling tools, and experimental design for fair comparisons.
subtopics: Measuring throughput: TFLOPs and the counting of operations
Utilization metrics: achieved vs theoretical peak
Benchmark design: varying batch, sequence length, and head dim
Profiling tools (Nsight, nvprof, CUPTI, vendor tracers) and counters
Ablation studies and controlled experiments

chapters.title: Chapter 18: GPU Software Ecosystem and Optimized Libraries
chapters.description: Surveys software frameworks and libraries used to implement and optimize attention and GEMM kernels, their abstractions, and how they map to hardware primitives.
subtopics: CUTLASS: building blocks for high-performance GEMM primitives
cuDNN and vendor-optimized primitives for attention/GEMM
Triton and other high-level kernel-generation frameworks
PyTorch integration points, kernels and extensions
Considerations for portability vs hardware-specific optimizations
